_about: THE WATER RULE's numbers (Track WS, 2026-10-10; scripts/sim/sea_rules.gd reads this, scripts/sim/world.gd applies it). A unit of domain 'sea' (data/units: patrol_boat, supply_boat) stays on water at least its draught_m deep. The World is given a water query (World.set_water: a Callable (x, y) -> metres of water, 0 or less on land) and, while it has one, checks every step a sea unit plans: the steps' arcs are sampled, and at each sample the hull's centre and both its ends must be over water at least draught deep. A step that would leave the water is CLAMPED the way the envelope clamps: first SLOWED (the same turn at slower and slower end speeds, down to the floor of the step's speed window), then, if even the slowest leaves the water, HELD (the unit stays where it is, speed 0); either way the step reports clamped with the limit 'shore'. Without a water query the rule is off (the sim is testable without the generator). EVERY VALUE HERE IS PROPOSED by Track WS; none is a decision.

hull_fraction._reason: the hull's ends are checked at this share of the unit's size_m ahead of and astern of its centre, along its heading: 0.5 is the bow and the stern. The water must be deep enough under all three points, so a 27 m boat's bow does not touch a shore its centre is 13 m from

sample_m._reason: a step's arc is sampled at least this often (and at least four times, however short): a boat's step is 12 to 25 m, so a spit or a rock 5 m wide is not stepped over

slow_tries._reason: a step that leaves the water is tried at this many slower end speeds, evenly spaced from the planned one down to the floor of the step's speed window, before the unit is held; four keeps the choice fine without searching
